step.title: Matrix inverse via Gauss-Jordan
step.objective: Can invert a 2×2 matrix by Gauss-Jordan
step.promptDraft: I'm a first-year engineering student. Walk me through inverting a 2×2 matrix with Gauss-Jordan elimination, one row operation per line. No greetings or small talk. Short structured bullets, max ~150 words, bold key terms. Then ask me one question to check I got it, and wait.

input.chatExcerpt:
[R] what is an inverse matrix
[L] The inverse A⁻¹ satisfies A·A⁻¹ = I. Not every matrix has one: A is invertible exactly when det(A) ≠ 0.
[R] why does det 0 mean no inverse
[L] If det(A) = 0 the columns are linearly dependent, so A squashes space into a lower dimension and you can't undo it.
[R] hmm ok kind of
[L] Think of it like flattening a 3D object into a sheet of paper — you lose information.
